newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU steelmakers regret U.S. dumping complaints.
newsitem.headline: EU steelmakers regret U.S. dumping complaints.

text.p: European steelmakers said on Thursday they deeply regretted a move by four U.S. steel rod producers and a union group to file a formal complaint about alleged dumping of products by the European Union and others.
"Eurofer is deeply dismayed and disappointed at the filing yesterday," the European Confederation of Iron and Steel Industries said in a statement.

"The complaints cover more than 90 percent of the imports from third countries of this product and must be seen as a clear demonstration of national trade laws, not as a means of defence but rather as protectionism," it added

The petition filed in Washington charged that stainless steel rod imports from Italy, Germany, Japan, Korea, Spain, Sweden and Taiwan are being sold in the United States at prices well below the product's home market value.

The petitioners, which account for almost all stainless steel rod production in the United States, requested that the U.S. government impose antidumping duties ranging up to 46 percent on the imports of stainless steel rods from those countries.
But the Europeans countered, stating that there had been no damage to the U.S. domestic industry.
Eurofer said domestic U.S. demand remained very strong and could not be met by local suppliers, and that therefore imports were filling a vital gap.

"Eurofer believes that the refusal of the U.S. Specialty Steel Industry to continue talks... and their rejection without discussion of the European proposals shows clearly that they have chosen to attempt to solve their problems through confrontation rather than dialogue," the European statement concluded. -- Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810, Fax +32 2 230 7710
